newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich asks Greenspan to help Congress raise GDP.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich asks Greenspan to help Congress raise GDP.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said on Friday he has asked Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to help Congress devise policies that would improve the real rate of economic growth.

Speaking at a press conference in his district office, the Georgia Republican said he wanted Congress' Joint Economic Committee to develop a series of hearings and to propose means to maximize American economic growth.

Gingrich said he spoke to Greenspan by telephone after telling business leaders earlier Friday that he would like to boost U.S. economic growth to between 4 percent and 5 percent annually. The Gross Domestic Product growth rate was an annual 3.8 percent in the fourth quarter, and most economists believe the current rate is at least at 3 percent.
"I was asking Alan if he would be willing to help us intellectually look at the model of what would maximize growth in the United States," the House speaker said.
Gingrich disclosed little about Greenspan's reaction, but said the Fed chairman was "deeply committed" to the highest possible real growth rate.

Gingrich emphasised that his discussion with Greenspan was not an attempt to get the central bank to be more open about economic growth following the Fed's quarter-point increase in interest rates last week.

"He made the point that we shouldn't get too locked into a specific number because the truth is the numbers are not very accurate, given the size of our economy and the complexity of it," Gingrich said.

After fielding repeated questions from reporters on the subject, Gingrich sought to play down the formality of his discussion with Greenspan. "He's an economist, I'm a historian," he said. "We talk about ideas, five or six times a year."
